out_items.name: No bare hand contact with ready-to-eat food, or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: when being asked about the fried onions, the CFM grabbed a handful of them with his bare hands.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. Discontinue handling foods with bare hands. The onions were discarded.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap at the 3-vat sink area handsink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: fried onions cooked yesterday were being held at room temperature.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. Cooked vegetables must be held either hot or cold and can’t be held at room temperature. The onions were discarded.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: there were containers of food with expired date marking dates in the walk-in. The vegetable curry was dated 6/11 (2 days past expiration date), chicken masala was dated 6/10 (3 days past), and cashew sauce was dated 6/8 (5 days past).
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. The EHS educated the PIC on keeping track of date marking dates. The products were discarded.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.title: Food Thermometers, Provided & Accessible
violations.observation: The certified food manager could not provide a food temperature measuring device. His food thermometer was located in the attic storage space, so it was not being used, and the batteries in it were dead.
violations.corrective_action: A metal-stemmed probe food thermometer shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures. The PIC ordered a new thermometer during the inspection to correct. RASOI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 06/18/2026) Page 2 of 3

violations.title: Thermometers, Location for Units with TCS foods
violations.observation: Two of the refrigeration units did not have thermometers in them. There were thermometers on the back of the unit, but these were not visible without moving the units.
violations.corrective_action: Cold or hot holding equipment used for the storage of time/temperature control for safety food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one integral or permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's temperature display. Obtain and install thermometers in these two units as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. Observed three containers of food stored on the floor in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. Discontinue storing foods on the floor. Correct as soon as possible or before, the next routine inspection not to exceed six months.

out_items.name: Wiping cloths properly used and stored

violations.title: Wiping Cloths Stored in Sanitizer Solution
violations.observation: Wet wiping cloths used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces were observed stored in water without any sanitizer.
violations.corrective_action: Wet wiping cloths are to be used for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces and are to be held in a chemical sanitizer solution at the appropriate concentration between uses. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. The PIC added bleach to the wiping cloth bucket.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: a large cylinder filled with soiled water and in-use utensils was stored on the counter. In-use utensils can’t be stored in soiled room temperature water. The water was 100°F.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Discontinue storing utensils in standing water unless the water is constantly at 135ºF. The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following equipment is not operating properly and/or is in poor repair: condensation is leaking into a pan inside the glass front one door refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Equipment shall be maintained in a state of repair and condition that meets the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2. Please have the refrigerator serviced so that the leak is repaired. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The EHS provided the manager with the health department model policy. CDI.

violations.title: No Bare Hand Contact with RTE Foods
violations.observation: Food employee(s) was observed handling the following ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands: when asked about a product in the kitchen, the CFM touched the food (“crispy chips”) with his bare hand.
violations.corrective_action: Except when washing fruits and vegetables, food employees may not contact ready-to-eat foods using their bare hands. Employees shall be using suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, or clean disposable gloves to handle all ready-to-eat foods. Proper handling of food and effective handwashing procedures will help prevent foodborne illness. The EHS discussed this with the food manager. CDI.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided in the men’s restroom, and two hand washing sinks in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The manager provided paper towels at each of the sinks during the inspection. RASOI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 12/22/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no hand soap in at the handsink next to the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. CDI

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw chicken was stored over ready to eat foods in the True one door refrigerator.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The manager moved the raw chicken during the inspection. CDI.

out_items.name: Proper cold holding temperatures

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: several products in the walk-in were not being held cold enough including: cut cabbage at 53º, cooked noodles at 53º, cooked rice at 52º, chili sauce 53º, red sauce 45º, yogurt at 51 and 57º, rice noodles at 52º, and ginger paste at 52º. upon arrival, several pots of raw meats (lamb and chicken) were thawing in standing water. The meats were 60ºF. Squeeze bottles of condiments made in house (yogurt sauce) were being stored in a very shallow ice bath and were 53ºF.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. All products listed above were discarded by the manager. The refrigerator was not working properly. The manager called a repair technician. The thawing meats were placed in the walk-in freezer to cool. In order for an ice bath to be effective in keeping foods cold, the ice must completely surround the container being stored in it. The manager moved the dressings to a refrigerator.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: there were numerous foods prepared on site that were not being date marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. Correct by the follow-up in ten days, by Friday, January 2, 2026.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: upon arrival, several pots of raw meats (lamb and chicken) were thawing in standing water.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. The manager moved the foods to the walk-in freezer to correct. CDI.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of yogurt sauce and other sauces were not labeled.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. All packages foods prepared on site must be labeled. Correct by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor
violations.observation: Food stored on the floor and/or food stored less than 6 inches off the floor. The thawing pots of meats were stored on the floor in the kitchen. Food was stored on the walk-in freezer floor.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food at least 6 inches off the floor on approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage.

violations.title: Packaged Food Display, No Direct Contact Water/Ice
violations.observation: The following packaged food was found stored in direct contact with ice: a grocery bag full of jalapeño peppers was stored in the ice in the ice machine.
violations.corrective_action: Packaged food may not be stored in direct contact with ice or water if the food is subject to the entry of water because of the nature of its packaging, wrapping, or container or its positioning in the ice or water. The manager moved the bag of jalapeños. CDI.

violations.title: Miscellaneous Source Contamination
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were found subject to contamination after receipt and during storage due to the condition as described: several spices and other food ingredients were stored on and around one of the handsinks in the kitchen, exposing them to splash while employees wash hands.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 through 3-306. The manager moved the food items from around the handsink. CDI.

out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: the rice spoon was being stored in standing water that was 106ºF. At the bar, the ice scoop handle was stored in the ice.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. The manager changed the water, but it as not hot enough. If storing utensils in standing water, the water must be at least 135ºF at all times. The manger moved the ice scoop.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Soiled Linens Properly Stored
violations.observation: Soiled linens were found stored in a location that may directly or indirectly contaminate food or food-contact surfaces. Visibly soiled linens ()white wiping cloths) were being used to clean food prep areas.
violations.corrective_action: Soiled linens shall be kept in clean, nonabsorbent receptacles or clean, washable laundry bags and stored and transported to prevent contamination of food, clean equipment, clean utensils, and single service items. The manager removed the soiled linens from use and put them in the wash.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Single-Service/Use Items, Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed that cases of single service items were stored on the floor, exposing them to contamination
violations.corrective_action: Store clean equipment, utensils, and linens in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. The staff moved the cases onto an approved dunnage rack during the inspection. RASOI INDIAN CUISINE (Inspection Date: 12/22/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The following refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain cold food at or below 41F: the ambient temperature of the walk-in was 56ºF and foods in the unit were not being held cold enough.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. The manager was aware of the problem with the walk-in and called a technician to service the unit.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Design/Construction
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not designed or constructed to be easily cleanable: the establishment was reusing food manufacturer 5 gallon buckets used to ship yogurt and other foods, to store foods made on site.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. Five gallon buckets are not approved for re-use and should be discarded after emptied of the original contents. Remove all unapproved 5 gallon buckets by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Cleaning Frequency
violations.observation: There was a foul odor coming from the grease trap area, located next to the three compartment sink.
violations.corrective_action: Clean the physical facilities at a frequency necessary to ensure the protection and safe preparation of food. The manager said the grease trap is cleaned monthly. Please check the grease trap again before the follow-up and clean it if necessary.

out_items.name: Food separated and protected

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: Observed raw chicken stored above raw salmon in 2 DR UC at expo.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). PIC was informed by handouts about policy on storage raw products due to different cook temperatures. PIC placed raw chicken below raw salmon.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: cooked chicken, cooked lentils, cooked lamb and etc.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS discussed date marking with management. All food sitting under refrigeration for more than 24 hours requires labels with dates. PIC labeled the food items during the inspection for compliance.

violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently.
